authored-by: Kai Lüttmann <33122946+KaiLuettmann@users.noreply.github.com>', 'fix(llm): preserve Gemini thought_signature through the AgentLoop dict path

#176 added the Gemini thought_signature round-trip but only covered the
in-memory AIMessage path its unit tests exercise. The AgentLoop replays
conversation history as OpenAI-format dicts, stamping the signature into
tool_calls[i].extra_content.google.thought_signature
(loop.py _attach_tool_call_thought_signatures).

LangChain's _convert_dict_to_message discards extra_content during the early
_convert_input step of invoke()/stream() -- before _get_request_payload
re-injects -- so _signature_maps reads an empty additional_kwargs and the
outbound request goes out unsigned. Gemini then rejects the next tool-using
turn with HTTP 400 "Function call is missing a thought_signature in
functionCall parts". This broke every tool-using loop turn on gemini-3.x
(single or parallel), e.g. the parallel load_skill case.

Override ChatOpenAIWithReasoning._convert_input -- the single chokepoint both
invoke and stream call while input is still raw dicts -- to lift signatures
back onto the converted AIMessage in the same
additional_kwargs["tool_call_thought_signatures"] shape the in-memory path
uses, so the existing _signature_maps / _inject_tool_call_thought_signatures
machinery handles both paths identically. Idempotent via an
isinstance(raw, dict) guard. No parallel-specific handling needed: Gemini
signs only the first of N parallel calls and that signature covers the block.

Add regression tests in TestChatOpenAIWithReasoningOutboundPayload that drive
the real dict path (the gap #176's tests missed): red without the fix
(KeyError: 'extra_content'), green with it.', 'feat(agent): persist run usage summary

fix(agent): make Stop responsive mid-stream and between tools (#229)

Symptom 2 of #229: clicking Stop during a run did nothing, or only took
effect after a long delay. The cancel signal (_cancelled bool) was polled
only at the top of the ReAct iteration loop, so a Stop pressed while the
agent was mid-LLM-stream or executing tools was ignored until the entire
current iteration — the whole streamed answer plus all its tool calls —
finished and the next iteration check ran.

Add cooperative cancel checkpoints at the granularity the user actually
waits on:

- Switch _cancelled to a threading.Event (_cancel_event) so the flag is
  safe to poll from the streaming thread.
- Thread a should_cancel predicate into ChatLLM.stream_chat; the per-chunk
  loop breaks as soon as it is set, so a live stream stops at the next
  token instead of running to completion.
- After the stream returns, check the flag before processing tool calls:
  a cancel during streaming ends the run immediately and discards the
  partial turn (no tools run).
- Check the flag at the top of _process_tool_calls and between tool batches
  in _batch_execute, so a multi-tool turn stops after the current tool
  rather than launching the rest.

Limitation (documented in the PR): a connection that hangs before emitting
any chunk leaves the worker blocked in a socket read, which Python cannot
interrupt cooperatively from another thread; that case stays bounded by the
existing client timeout (TIMEOUT_SECONDS). Cancel now lands promptly in all
the normal "working" states (tokens streaming, tools running).

no-op); loop-level cancel mid-stream ends the run as cancelled and skips
tool execution. Full suite: 3199 passed, 2 skipped.

fix(security): block CGNAT/mesh ranges in SSRF guard; close QQ media redirect-to-internal

Two SSRF gaps in the channel media-fetch path:

1. channels/utils._is_private only checked is_loopback | is_link_local |
   is_private. ipaddress.is_private is False for RFC 6598 shared address
   space (100.64.0.0/10 — the default Tailscale/mesh range), so those hosts
   passed validate_url_target and every channel (QQ, DingTalk, NapCat,
   Telegram, channelsui) would fetch them as media. Switch to
   `not addr.is_global or addr.is_multicast`, which blocks all
   non-globally-routable ranges uniformly and also closes an IPv4-multicast
   gap (is_global is True for multicast). Matches web_reader_tool._url_allowed.

2. qq._read_media_bytes validated media_ref once, then fetched with
   allow_redirects=True. media_ref is agent-controlled (from msg.media, which
   is routinely influenced by untrusted external content), so a public URL
   returning 302 -> http://169.254.169.254/... would be followed unchecked and
   the internal body uploaded as a media attachment. Set allow_redirects=False
   and fail closed on 3xx, mirroring napcat.py. (The separate inbound download
   at qq.py:618 fetches a trusted QQ CDN URL and is intentionally left as-is.)

Adds agent/tests/test_url_target_security.py covering both fixes. The central
guard (validate_url_target / _is_private) previously had no tests at all.

Add channel-agnostic session reset support to ChannelRuntime so all 16
IM adapters (Feishu, Discord, Telegram, Slack, DingTalk, WeChat, WeCom,
QQ, NapCat, Matrix, WhatsApp, Signal, MS Teams, Email, Mochat, WebSocket)
gain /new, /reset, and /newsession commands without individual adapter
changes.

## Summary

- Intercept /new, /reset, /newsession in ChannelRuntime._handle_inbound()
  before session routing, clearing the session_key mapping so the next
  message creates a fresh session
- Add reset_session(session_key) method to remove mapping and persist
- Add _is_new_session_command() static method for command detection
- 5 new regression tests covering reset flow, no-session edge case,
  alias commands, substring non-interception, and persistence

## Why

IM channel users had no way to reset their conversation session. The
ChannelRuntime._session_for() method permanently maps channel:chat_id
to session_id with no invalidation mechanism. Even Discord and Telegram
adapters that registered /new commands forwarded them as plain text to
the agent loop, which treated them as user prompts rather than session
management commands.

## Changes

- agent/src/channels/runtime.py: +35 lines
  - reset_session(): remove session_key from _session_map, persist
  - _is_new_session_command(): match /new, /reset, /newsession (case-insensitive)
  - _handle_inbound(): intercept before _session_for(), reply confirmation
- agent/tests/test_channels_runtime.py: +187 lines (5 tests)

The /correlation endpoint passed user input straight to the data loaders,
which key US/HK/A-share instruments by exchange-suffixed symbols
(AAPL.US / 0700.HK / 600000.SH). Bare tickers — exactly what the UI hint
suggests (e.g. "BTC-USDT,ETH-USDT,AAPL,SPY") — matched no loader and the
request failed with "Could not fetch price data for at least 2 assets.
Fetched: []".

Three layered fixes:

1. infer_market: classify by explicit suffix first, then bare numeric
   codes by digit length (6 digits = A-share, <=5 = HK). The old prefix
   heuristics misrouted bare HK codes (0700 -> SZ, 9988 -> US), ChiNext
   codes (300750 -> HK), and even suffixed 830799.BJ (-> US).
2. _normalize_symbol (new): canonicalize bare tickers to the loader
   symbol form before fetching, keeping the user's input as the label.
3. Fetch loop: walk the market's full FALLBACK_CHAIN until a loader
   actually returns data instead of stopping at the first *available*
   one, and log every per-source failure instead of the bare
   "except: continue" that made this failure mode undiagnosable.

Tests: +10 cases (bare/suffixed classification, symbol normalization,
chain fall-through); 22 pass.

The agent's trading_place_order tool could never place a share-quantity
order. LLMs routinely populate both sizing fields, leaving the unused one

the connector as non-None and place_order rejected the request with
"provide exactly one of quantity or notional".

preserving the "exactly one of quantity/notional" contract regardless of
which field the model over-fills.

fix(correlation): resolve bare tickers so the matrix stops failing with "Fetched: []"

The /correlation endpoint passed user input straight to the data loaders,
which key US/HK/A-share instruments by exchange-suffixed symbols
(AAPL.US / 0700.HK / 600000.SH). Bare tickers — exactly what the UI hint
suggests (e.g. "BTC-USDT,ETH-USDT,AAPL,SPY") — matched no loader and the
request failed with "Could not fetch price data for at least 2 assets.
Fetched: []".

Three layered fixes:

1. infer_market: classify by explicit suffix first, then bare numeric
   codes by digit length (6 digits = A-share, <=5 = HK). The old prefix
   heuristics misrouted bare HK codes (0700 -> SZ, 9988 -> US), ChiNext
   codes (300750 -> HK), and even suffixed 830799.BJ (-> US).
2. _normalize_symbol (new): canonicalize bare tickers to the loader
   symbol form before fetching, keeping the user's input as the label.
3. Fetch loop: walk the market's full FALLBACK_CHAIN until a loader
   actually returns data instead of stopping at the first *available*
   one, and log every per-source failure instead of the bare
   "except: continue" that made this failure mode undiagnosable.

Tests: +10 cases (bare/suffixed classification, symbol normalization,
chain fall-through); 22 pass.

## Problem

The previous shared-connection pool was incompatible with the agent's
parallel tool executor (ThreadPoolExecutor, up to 8 workers).  When the
agent fired 15 trading_quote calls in one iteration every worker thread
raced into the same `ib_async.IB` socket.  `ib_async` is not
thread-safe — its internal event loop is bound to one thread — so the
parallel access deadlocked the market-data stream.  Every session trace
ended with tool_call events but zero tool_result events for quotes.

Additionally, `get_quote` called `reqMktData` with `snapshot=False`
(streaming subscription) followed by a 2-second sleep and manual cancel.
This held the connection for 2+ seconds per symbol even when it worked.

## Solution

Two changes in `agent/src/trading/connectors/ibkr/local.py`:

1. **`reqMktData(..., snapshot=True)`** — requests a one-shot snapshot
   instead of a streaming subscription.  No sleep needed; the ticker
   delivers one tick and auto-cancels.  Drops the `_sleep(2.0)` and
   `cancelMktData` dance entirely.

2. **Thread-local pool** — replaces the shared `_TwsPool` with a
   `threading.local()`-based design:

   - Each worker thread gets its own `ib_async.IB` socket.
   - Unique client IDs via `itertools.count` + base config ID.
   - Per-thread reference counting so the connection persists across
     multiple tool calls in the same thread and disconnects only when
     the refcount drops to zero.
   - No socket is ever shared across threads — respects ib_async's
     single-thread-per-socket design.

Implement a signal engine for RVNL trend-recovery strategy with allocation and various parameters.', 'fix strict India data route', 'feat(agent): add stream retry configuration', 'feat(loaders): add Binance crypto fallback', "fix(ibkr): replace per-call connect/disconnect with thread-safe connection pool

## Problem
The local IBKR connector opened a fresh `ib_async.IB()` connection and
disconnected it on every single tool call (get_account_snapshot,
get_positions, get_open_orders, get_quote, get_historical_bars).  When
the agent invoked multiple trading tools in parallel every call reused
the same hard-coded client ID (77), which caused TWS / IB Gateway to
reject the duplicates with error 326:

    Unable to connect as the client id is already in use.
    Peer closed connection. clientId 77 already in use?

This made the connector unreliable under the agent's parallel execution
model and surfaced as intermittent `TimeOutError` and `Could not
connect to TWS / IB Gateway` errors in the CLI and Web UI.

## Solution
Replace the module-level `_connect()` / `_disconnect()` helpers with
a thread-safe connection pool class `_TwsPool` backed by a
`threading.Lock` and reference counting.

- `_pool.acquire(config)` connects once on first use; subsequent
  concurrent callers reuse the same `ib_async.IB` socket without
  reconnecting.
- `_pool.release()` decrements the refcount; the underlying socket is
  disconnected only when the last active caller releases.
- Guards against mid-flight profile switching (different host / port /
  profile) with a clear error instead of a silent misconfiguration.

All five public functions updated to use `_pool.acquire(cfg)` /
`_pool.release()`.  Call-site contract is unchanged — same
`try: … finally: _pool.release()` pattern.

## Impact
- No more client-ID collision errors under parallel agent call patterns.
- No resource leak from orphaned `ib_async.IB` instances.
- All 10 existing `test_ibkr_local.py` tests pass without modification.", 'fix(ibkr): restore tick-wait in get_quote and add timing + concurrency tests

## Problem 1: Empty ticker in get_quote (timing regression)

Commit b88df78 changed reqMktData(..., snapshot=True) to avoid the
2-second sleep and thread-safety deadlock, but the ib_async documentation
states: "The ticker will initially be empty and gradually (after a couple
of seconds) be filled" -- even with snapshot mode.  Reading the ticker
fields immediately after reqMktData returned None for bid/ask/last in
production, silently breaking all quote-dependent analysis.

## Problem 2: Existing test hid the bug

The _FakeIB.reqMktData mock returned a fully-populated ticker instantly
(bid=100.0, ask=100.2, ...), so the timing regression never surfaced in
CI.  The existing test_quote_and_history_are_readonly test passed despite
the bug.

## Solution

### agent/src/trading/connectors/ibkr/local.py

- Added _wait_for_tick(ib, ticker) helper that pumps the ib_async event
  loop via ib.waitOnUpdate() in 100 ms increments until at least one of
  bid/ask/last is populated, with a configurable 2-second timeout.
  Falls back to ib.sleep() for ib_async versions without waitOnUpdate.
- get_quote now calls _wait_for_tick() immediately after
  reqMktData(snapshot=True), ensuring the ticker fields are filled
  before serializing the quote response.
- Moved import itertools to the top-level import block (was previously
  added inline before the _TwsPool class in commit b88df78).

### agent/tests/test_ibkr_local.py -- 5 new tests

Timing tests (2):
- test_quote_waits_for_tick_arrival -- mock returns an initially-empty
  ticker; the wait loop runs without hanging, exits gracefully (fields
  stay None if data never arrives -- no deadlock).
- test_quote_receives_tick_after_event_loop_pump -- simulates the real
  async-tick flow: ticker starts empty, after 2 event-loop pumps
  _obj_get is patched to return populated values.  Asserts bid=150.0,
  ask=150.5, last=150.25 are correctly read after the wait loop.

Thread-local pool concurrency tests (3):
- test_pool_thread_local_isolation -- 4 concurrent threads acquire the
  pool via ThreadPoolExecutor with threading.Barrier to force distinct
  worker threads.  Each thread gets a unique client ID (> base 77) and
  a distinct ib_async.IB object.  Verifies no cross-thread leakage.
- test_pool_refcount_disconnects_on_last_release -- nested
  acquire/release in the same thread: disconnect is called only when
  the refcount reaches zero after the final release.
- test_pool_release_idempotent_no_connection -- calling release() on an
  empty pool is a safe no-op.

## Impact

- Quotes now work correctly in production -- ticker fields are populated
  before reading.
- All 10 existing + 5 new = 15 tests pass.
- The wait loop adds ~100-300 ms per quote in the common case (tick
  arrives quickly), with a 2-second safety ceiling.', 'fix(swarm): save nested output files safely

Add optional max_per_name, groups, and max_per_group parameters to the

constraints on each rebalance:

  w_i <= max_per_name                  (per-name cap)
  sum_{i in group_g} w_i <= max_per_group[g]  (per-group cap)

  optimizer: turnover_aware
  optimizer_params:

    max_per_name: 0.25
    groups:
      AAPL: tech
      MSFT: tech
    max_per_group:

The single ib.sleep(2.0) call in _wait_for_tick was unreliable when

fix(ibkr): use snapshot quotes and thread-local connection pool

## Problem

The previous shared-connection pool was incompatible with the agent's
parallel tool executor (ThreadPoolExecutor, up to 8 workers).  When the
agent fired 15 trading_quote calls in one iteration every worker thread
raced into the same `ib_async.IB` socket.  `ib_async` is not
thread-safe — its internal event loop is bound to one thread — so the
parallel access deadlocked the market-data stream.  Every session trace
ended with tool_call events but zero tool_result events for quotes.

Additionally, `get_quote` called `reqMktData` with `snapshot=False`
(streaming subscription) followed by a 2-second sleep and manual cancel.
This held the connection for 2+ seconds per symbol even when it worked.

## Solution

Two changes in `agent/src/trading/connectors/ibkr/local.py`:

1. **`reqMktData(..., snapshot=True)`** — requests a one-shot snapshot
   instead of a streaming subscription.  No sleep needed; the ticker
   delivers one tick and auto-cancels.  Drops the `_sleep(2.0)` and
   `cancelMktData` dance entirely.

2. **Thread-local pool** — replaces the shared `_TwsPool` with a
   `threading.local()`-based design:

   - Each worker thread gets its own `ib_async.IB` socket.
   - Unique client IDs via `itertools.count` + base config ID.
   - Per-thread reference counting so the connection persists across
     multiple tool calls in the same thread and disconnects only when
     the refcount drops to zero.
   - No socket is ever shared across threads — respects ib_async's
     single-thread-per-socket design.

## Impact

- No more hangs when the agent fires parallel trading_quote calls.
- Quotations complete in ~100 ms instead of 2+ seconds.
- All 10 `test_ibkr_local.py` tests pass without modification.

fix(backtest): validate validation-config knobs instead of crashing

The three validation tools read count/seed knobs straight from user
config["validation"] via run_validation, but none validated them:

  - walk_forward n_windows=0  -> ZeroDivisionError (len // n_windows)
  - walk_forward n_windows<0  -> silently returns empty windows with a
                                 NaN return_mean and negative consistency_rate
  - monte_carlo n_simulations<1 -> ZeroDivisionError (count / n_simulations)
  - monte_carlo/bootstrap seed<0 -> ValueError from np.random.default_rng
  - bootstrap n_bootstrap<1   -> IndexError from np.percentile on empty array
  - bootstrap confidence outside (0,1) -> ValueError from np.percentile

A single misconfigured knob either aborted the whole backtest with an
opaque error or returned NaN-laden garbage with no signal. Guard each knob
at function entry and return the same {"error": ...} shape these functions
already use for insufficient data, so a bad knob surfaces cleanly in the
validation results instead of crashing or silently corrupting the run.

fix(ibkr): replace per-call connect/disconnect with thread-safe connection pool

## Problem
The local IBKR connector opened a fresh `ib_async.IB()` connection and
disconnected it on every single tool call (get_account_snapshot,
get_positions, get_open_orders, get_quote, get_historical_bars).  When
the agent invoked multiple trading tools in parallel every call reused
the same hard-coded client ID (77), which caused TWS / IB Gateway to
reject the duplicates with error 326:

    Unable to connect as the client id is already in use.
    Peer closed connection. clientId 77 already in use?

This made the connector unreliable under the agent's parallel execution
model and surfaced as intermittent `TimeOutError` and `Could not
connect to TWS / IB Gateway` errors in the CLI and Web UI.

## Solution
Replace the module-level `_connect()` / `_disconnect()` helpers with
a thread-safe connection pool class `_TwsPool` backed by a
`threading.Lock` and reference counting.

- `_pool.acquire(config)` connects once on first use; subsequent
  concurrent callers reuse the same `ib_async.IB` socket without
  reconnecting.
- `_pool.release()` decrements the refcount; the underlying socket is
  disconnected only when the last active caller releases.
- Guards against mid-flight profile switching (different host / port /
  profile) with a clear error instead of a silent misconfiguration.

All five public functions updated to use `_pool.acquire(cfg)` /
`_pool.release()`.  Call-site contract is unchanged — same
`try: … finally: _pool.release()` pattern.

## Impact
- No more client-ID collision errors under parallel agent call patterns.
- No resource leak from orphaned `ib_async.IB` instances.
- All 10 existing `test_ibkr_local.py` tests pass without modification.
fix(ibkr): restore tick-wait in get_quote and add timing + concurrency tests

## Problem 1: Empty ticker in get_quote (timing regression)

Commit b88df78 changed reqMktData(..., snapshot=True) to avoid the
2-second sleep and thread-safety deadlock, but the ib_async documentation
states: "The ticker will initially be empty and gradually (after a couple
of seconds) be filled" -- even with snapshot mode.  Reading the ticker
fields immediately after reqMktData returned None for bid/ask/last in
production, silently breaking all quote-dependent analysis.

## Problem 2: Existing test hid the bug

The _FakeIB.reqMktData mock returned a fully-populated ticker instantly
(bid=100.0, ask=100.2, ...), so the timing regression never surfaced in
CI.  The existing test_quote_and_history_are_readonly test passed despite
the bug.

## Solution

### agent/src/trading/connectors/ibkr/local.py

- Added _wait_for_tick(ib, ticker) helper that pumps the ib_async event
  loop via ib.waitOnUpdate() in 100 ms increments until at least one of
  bid/ask/last is populated, with a configurable 2-second timeout.
  Falls back to ib.sleep() for ib_async versions without waitOnUpdate.
- get_quote now calls _wait_for_tick() immediately after
  reqMktData(snapshot=True), ensuring the ticker fields are filled
  before serializing the quote response.
- Moved import itertools to the top-level import block (was previously
  added inline before the _TwsPool class in commit b88df78).

### agent/tests/test_ibkr_local.py -- 5 new tests

Timing tests (2):
- test_quote_waits_for_tick_arrival -- mock returns an initially-empty
  ticker; the wait loop runs without hanging, exits gracefully (fields
  stay None if data never arrives -- no deadlock).
- test_quote_receives_tick_after_event_loop_pump -- simulates the real
  async-tick flow: ticker starts empty, after 2 event-loop pumps
  _obj_get is patched to return populated values.  Asserts bid=150.0,
  ask=150.5, last=150.25 are correctly read after the wait loop.

Thread-local pool concurrency tests (3):
- test_pool_thread_local_isolation -- 4 concurrent threads acquire the
  pool via ThreadPoolExecutor with threading.Barrier to force distinct
  worker threads.  Each thread gets a unique client ID (> base 77) and
  a distinct ib_async.IB object.  Verifies no cross-thread leakage.
- test_pool_refcount_disconnects_on_last_release -- nested
  acquire/release in the same thread: disconnect is called only when
  the refcount reaches zero after the final release.
- test_pool_release_idempotent_no_connection -- calling release() on an
  empty pool is a safe no-op.

## Impact

- Quotes now work correctly in production -- ticker fields are populated
  before reading.
- All 10 existing + 5 new = 15 tests pass.
- The wait loop adds ~100-300 ms per quote in the common case (tick
  arrives quickly), with a 2-second safety ceiling.

fix(backtest): keep backtest outputs finite and validation.json strict

Two related non-finite-output robustness gaps:

1. initial_cash is not validated. BacktestConfigSchema uses extra="allow"
   and never declares initial_cash, so a config with initial_cash=0 (or
   negative) passes validation and reaches calc_metrics, where
   `equity[-1] / initial_cash - 1` yields inf total_return / annual_return.
   Declare initial_cash: float = Field(default=1_000_000, gt=0) so a
   non-positive value is rejected at the config boundary (the CLI runner and
   the MCP backtest tool both run through this schema).

2. The in-engine validation.json write bypassed strict-JSON serialization.
   run_card and the standalone `python -m backtest.validation` both sanitize
   with _json_safe + allow_nan=False, but BaseEngine.run_backtest wrote
   json.dumps(v_results, ...) with the default allow_nan=True. A non-finite
   validation metric therefore produced bare NaN/Infinity tokens (invalid
   RFC-8259 JSON) only on the automatic in-engine path. Extract the strict
   write into a shared write_validation_json helper and call it from both the
   engine and the standalone main so every writer of validation.json emits
   the same valid JSON (non-finite -> null).

write_validation_json serializes inf/NaN as null and parses under a strict

fix(ibkr): replace fixed 2s sleep with ib.sleep() polling loop that exits on real data

The single ib.sleep(2.0) call in _wait_for_tick was unreliable when
multiple quotes ran in parallel via ThreadPoolExecutor (8 workers).
Each thread has its own IB connection (thread-local pool), but the
fixed 2s sleep doesn't account for varying network latency -- some
ticks arrive in 200ms, others take longer, and 2s wasn't always
enough, causing empty/NaN fields in 7/10 parallel quote requests.

Replace with incremental ib.sleep(0.1) polling that checks
_tick_has_data after each pump and exits as soon as real market data
arrives, with a 5s total timeout. This gives each ticker dedicated
event-loop time and avoids the race where the LLM reads partial data.

Key: uses ib.sleep() NOT waitOnUpdate() for polling -- ib.sleep
reliably processes all pending socket messages, while waitOnUpdate
can return True for unrelated messages on the same connection.

Changes:
- Re-add _tick_has_data() with None + NaN rejection
- Rewrite _wait_for_tick() as ib.sleep(0.1) polling loop (5s timeout)
- Add test_quote_waits_for_delayed_tick_arrival: tick arrives after
  5 pump cycles, verifies correct bid/ask/last values
- Add test_quote_keeps_polling_when_ticker_is_nan: fields start NaN,
  continue polling until real data (200.0) arrives after 8 pumps

Signed-off-by: dependabot[bot] <support@github.com>', 'fix(frontend): prevent insertBefore DOM race during streaming output

During streaming, the chat UI rendered two separate conditional blocks
(pre-stream placeholder and live streaming area) that mounted/unmounted
independently based on state transitions. When reasoningActive switched
to streamingText, React had to simultaneously unmount one div and mount
another, while scrollToBottom requestAnimationFrame inserted DOM
operations between React reconciliation cycles, causing the reference
node to disappear and triggering an insertBefore NotFoundError.

Fix by merging both blocks into a single stable wrapper div that only
checks status === streaming, with inner conditionals controlling
which content is shown. The wrapper itself never unmounts during
streaming, eliminating the DOM race.

Also debounce ConversationTimeline scroll handler DOM queries with
requestAnimationFrame to avoid conflicts with React batched updates.

Signed-off-by: Yufeng He <40085740+he-yufeng@users.noreply.github.com>', 'fix(fundamentals): dedup restated rows and prevent period regression in PIT snapshots

Two point-in-time correctness bugs in tushare_fundamentals.py:

1. `query_fundamentals` did not deduplicate after the PIT cut, so the same
   (ts_code, end_date) could appear twice when both the original filing and a
   later restatement were visible as of the query date.  Fix: after the PIT
   cut, keep only the row with the latest effective pit date per
   (ts_code, end_date); ties preserve the last row in input order (natural
   Tushare ordering where restatements follow originals).

2. `enrich_price_frames_with_fundamentals` fed the deduped snapshot directly
   into merge_asof.  This caused two problems: (a) the per-day PIT visibility
   was evaluated on already-deduped data, making a restatement whose pit_date
   was in the future appear as if it were always visible; (b) when a late
   restatement for an *older* period (end_date < currently-visible end_date)
   arrived, merge_asof picked it as the nearest-prior announcement, regressing
   every subsequent snapshot to the older period.

   Fix: enrich now calls the new internal `_query_pit_cut` (raw PIT cut, no
   dedup) and builds an explicit forward-only effective timeline — a row is
   only accepted into the timeline when its end_date >= the currently-visible
   end_date.  Same-period restatements (same end_date, later pit_date) pass
   this check and appear as additional timeline entries; merge_asof then
   surfaces the restatement value only from its own pit_date onward.

Fixes #771

The GHSA-p3c9 guard wrapped network MCP transports in Starlette's
TrustedHostMiddleware, whose plain split(":") Host parsing mangles
bracketed IPv6 ([::1]:8900 -> "[") and matches case-sensitively. An
MCP server bound to --host ::1 rejected every request with 400, and no
VIBE_TRADING_MCP_ALLOWED_HOSTS entry ([::1] or ::1) could fix it — the
only way out was '*', disabling the protection entirely. LOCALHOST was
rejected the same way, while the Origin guard (urlparse().hostname)
already lowercased, so the two layers disagreed.

Replace the middleware with a repo-owned _HostGuardMiddleware that
normalizes the header (brackets/port stripped, bare IPv6 kept whole,
lowercased) before matching the allow-list, normalize configured
entries the same way, and add ::1 to the loopback default. Allow-list
semantics (exact, *. wildcard, *) and the 400 rejection are unchanged;
the Origin guard is untouched.

Refs GHSA-p3c9

loader's validate_ohlc drops any bar with a non-positive OHLC value and the
engine rejects any open at price <= 0. On real EU power data this silently
deletes ~27% of DE-LU days (every bar with a sub-zero hourly-derived low),
punching holes in rolling statistics (e.g. a z-score entry signal) with no
warning.

Add an opt-in `allow_nonpositive_prices` flag (default False — existing
behavior byte-identical for all positive-price markets):

- loaders/base.py: validate_ohlc gains the flag. Structural invariants
  (high<low, high/low bracketing open/close) always enforced; when the flag
  is set, negative prices pass through and only an exactly-zero price is
  rejected. Zero is genuinely undefined for `size = notional / price` and
  margin; a negative price is well-defined via abs().
- engines/base.py: BaseEngine reads the flag from config. _plan_open_order
  rejects an exactly-zero open always, negatives only when the flag is off.
  _calc_raw_size / _calc_margin divide by abs(price) so a negative entry
  price yields a positive size magnitude (direction carries the sign) and
  positive collateral — unchanged for positive prices. _calc_pnl already
  uses a price difference, well-defined through zero.

Tests open a position on a negative-price bar and assert size/margin/PnL are
well-defined through zero, that an exactly-zero price is still rejected with
the flag on, and that the default still rejects negatives. A regression test
pins *why* zero stays dropped rather than kept: a surviving 0.00 close yields
inf at the `close.pct_change().fillna(0.0)` sites in benchmark.py and
engines/base.py (fillna fills NaN, not inf), so keeping it would corrupt the
return series. Fixture carries the 5 real non-positive-close bars from a 2025
NO2/DE-LU window (ENTSO-E via Energy-Charts / Bundesnetzagentur | SMARD,
CC BY 4.0). Existing engine and OHLC-validation suites pass unchanged
(140 tests total).

fix(news): handle Windows CRLF checkout for manifest digest validation

Git on Windows auto-converts LF -> CRLF on checkout, which breaks the
pinned SHA256 manifest check in load_catalog().  Two layers of defense:

1. .gitattributes pins upstream_manifest.json to LF eol so Git never
   rewrites it to CRLF.

2. _canonical_manifest_bytes() normalizes bytes back to LF before
   computing the digest and parsing JSON, so the check still passes even
   if the file was already checked out with CRLF (e.g. on a pre-existing
   clone before the .gitattributes was committed).

Also fixes a stray whitespace in ConsolePage.vue template.

退出时应用卡死、必须强制退出的根因是双重无限等待：

- Python 侧 uvicorn.run 未设 timeout_graceful_shutdown（默认 None），
  收到 SIGTERM 后无限等待活跃 SSE/keep-alive 连接关闭，进程不退出；
- Rust 侧 sidecar::terminate 用无超时的 child.wait() 等待 Python 退出，
  阻塞在 RunEvent::ExitRequested 回调（Tauri 主事件循环线程）上，
  导致窗口无法销毁、进程无法退出。

修复（分层防御）：
- api_server.py: uvicorn 增加 timeout_graceful_shutdown=5
- sidecar.rs: unix terminate 改为 SIGTERM + 限时 try_wait 轮询，
  超 5s 则 killpg(SIGKILL) 兜底回收；新增 unix 回归测试验证
  SIGTERM 被忽略时能在 5s 内强杀回收。

field validates to a real datetime object and would hit the same
failure one level down.

output schema shaped like this (plain object properties, no
additionalProperties, nested datetime field): old _make_jsonable raises
the reported Circular reference detected error; the patched version
serializes correctly, verified both from direct construction and via
pydantic.TypeAdapter validation (the path fastmcp's client actually

fix(frontend): prevent insertBefore DOM race during streaming output

During streaming, the chat UI rendered two separate conditional blocks
(pre-stream placeholder and live streaming area) that mounted/unmounted
independently based on state transitions. When reasoningActive switched
to streamingText, React had to simultaneously unmount one div and mount
another, while scrollToBottom requestAnimationFrame inserted DOM
operations between React reconciliation cycles, causing the reference
node to disappear and triggering an insertBefore NotFoundError.

Fix by merging both blocks into a single stable wrapper div that only
checks status === streaming, with inner conditionals controlling
which content is shown. The wrapper itself never unmounts during
streaming, eliminating the DOM race.

Also debounce ConversationTimeline scroll handler DOM queries with
requestAnimationFrame to avoid conflicts with React batched updates.

fix(fundamentals): dedup restated rows and prevent period regression in PIT snapshots

Two point-in-time correctness bugs in tushare_fundamentals.py:

1. `query_fundamentals` did not deduplicate after the PIT cut, so the same
   (ts_code, end_date) could appear twice when both the original filing and a
   later restatement were visible as of the query date.  Fix: after the PIT
   cut, keep only the row with the latest effective pit date per
   (ts_code, end_date); ties preserve the last row in input order (natural
   Tushare ordering where restatements follow originals).

2. `enrich_price_frames_with_fundamentals` fed the deduped snapshot directly
   into merge_asof.  This caused two problems: (a) the per-day PIT visibility
   was evaluated on already-deduped data, making a restatement whose pit_date
   was in the future appear as if it were always visible; (b) when a late
   restatement for an *older* period (end_date < currently-visible end_date)
   arrived, merge_asof picked it as the nearest-prior announcement, regressing
   every subsequent snapshot to the older period.

   Fix: enrich now calls the new internal `_query_pit_cut` (raw PIT cut, no
   dedup) and builds an explicit forward-only effective timeline — a row is
   only accepted into the timeline when its end_date >= the currently-visible
   end_date.  Same-period restatements (same end_date, later pit_date) pass
   this check and appear as additional timeline entries; merge_asof then
   surfaces the restatement value only from its own pit_date onward.

Fixes #771

fix(mcp): accept IPv6 and case-variant hosts in the network guard

The GHSA-p3c9 guard wrapped network MCP transports in Starlette's
TrustedHostMiddleware, whose plain split(":") Host parsing mangles
bracketed IPv6 ([::1]:8900 -> "[") and matches case-sensitively. An
MCP server bound to --host ::1 rejected every request with 400, and no
VIBE_TRADING_MCP_ALLOWED_HOSTS entry ([::1] or ::1) could fix it — the
only way out was '*', disabling the protection entirely. LOCALHOST was
rejected the same way, while the Origin guard (urlparse().hostname)
already lowercased, so the two layers disagreed.

Replace the middleware with a repo-owned _HostGuardMiddleware that
normalizes the header (brackets/port stripped, bare IPv6 kept whole,
lowercased) before matching the allow-list, normalize configured
entries the same way, and add ::1 to the loopback default. Allow-list
semantics (exact, *. wildcard, *) and the 400 rejection are unchanged;
the Origin guard is untouched.

Refs GHSA-p3c9

fix(backtest): consume historical USD-M funding + round settlement jitter

Two fixes that make historical funding actually flow into perp backtests:

1. Loader: Binance funding settlement timestamps carry millisecond
   jitter (e.g. 2026-05-05T08:00:00.011Z). The raw timestamps never
   intersect bar timestamps, so the missing-settlement guard raises
   'funding settlement data is missing' for most real fetches. Round
   settlement timestamps to the second before aligning.

2. Engine: the loader writes a historical funding_rate column into the
   frame, but calc_crypto_funding_fee still charges the fixed config
   rate (default 0.0001) — the fetched data is never consumed. Prefer
   the bar's historical rate when present and finite; fall back to the
   fixed rate otherwise (spot-proxy and daily-fallback paths keep
   their existing behaviour).

Verified against live Binance USD-M data (BTC/ETH -USDT-PERP, 4H,
Jan-Jul 2026): fixed-rate short returned +44.5%, historical-funding
short +39.1% — the ~5pp delta matches 2026's predominantly negative
funding regime where shorts pay.

Tests: jitter alignment test in test_ccxt_perpetual_loader.py; three
override/fallback tests in test_crypto_engine.py.

fix(shadow): skip the entry-hour gate on daily bars

Rules mined from real journals carry an entry_hour window from actual
fill times (p10-p90, e.g. 9-11 for market-hours trading). The generated
signal engine replays on daily bars stamped at midnight, so gating on
bar_hour rejected every bar: any profile mined from real intraday fills
produced a silently flat strategy with zero entries and no error.

On daily (or coarser) bars the mined hour window carries no
information, so the generated engine now applies it only when the bar
index has more than one distinct time-of-day (intraday data). Other
rule conditions (RSI, prior return, holding) are unchanged.

Regression tests cover: market-hours window entering on midnight daily
bars, intraday data still enforcing the window, and date-only journal
windows ({0, 0}) still entering.

Add allow_nonpositive_prices: open on negative-price bars, still reject zero

Markets like European day-ahead power clear negative routinely, but the
loader's validate_ohlc drops any bar with a non-positive OHLC value and the
engine rejects any open at price <= 0. On real EU power data this silently
deletes ~27% of DE-LU days (every bar with a sub-zero hourly-derived low),
punching holes in rolling statistics (e.g. a z-score entry signal) with no
warning.

Add an opt-in `allow_nonpositive_prices` flag (default False — existing
behavior byte-identical for all positive-price markets):

- loaders/base.py: validate_ohlc gains the flag. Structural invariants
  (high<low, high/low bracketing open/close) always enforced; when the flag
  is set, negative prices pass through and only an exactly-zero price is
  rejected. Zero is genuinely undefined for `size = notional / price` and
  margin; a negative price is well-defined via abs().
- engines/base.py: BaseEngine reads the flag from config. _plan_open_order
  rejects an exactly-zero open always, negatives only when the flag is off.
  _calc_raw_size / _calc_margin divide by abs(price) so a negative entry
  price yields a positive size magnitude (direction carries the sign) and
  positive collateral — unchanged for positive prices. _calc_pnl already
  uses a price difference, well-defined through zero.

Tests open a position on a negative-price bar and assert size/margin/PnL are
well-defined through zero, that an exactly-zero price is still rejected with
the flag on, and that the default still rejects negatives. A regression test
pins *why* zero stays dropped rather than kept: a surviving 0.00 close yields
inf at the `close.pct_change().fillna(0.0)` sites in benchmark.py and
engines/base.py (fillna fills NaN, not inf), so keeping it would corrupt the
return series. Fixture carries the 5 real non-positive-close bars from a 2025
NO2/DE-LU window (ENTSO-E via Energy-Charts / Bundesnetzagentur | SMARD,
CC BY 4.0). Existing engine and OHLC-validation suites pass unchanged
(140 tests total).

Git on Windows auto-converts LF -> CRLF on checkout, which breaks the
pinned SHA256 manifest check in load_catalog().  Two layers of defense:

   rewrites it to CRLF.

2. _canonical_manifest_bytes() normalizes bytes back to LF before
   computing the digest and parsing JSON, so the check still passes even
   if the file was already checked out with CRLF (e.g. on a pre-existing
   clone before the .gitattributes was committed).

fix(desktop): prevent quit hang via sidecar graceful-shutdown timeout

退出时应用卡死、必须强制退出的根因是双重无限等待：

- Python 侧 uvicorn.run 未设 timeout_graceful_shutdown（默认 None），
  收到 SIGTERM 后无限等待活跃 SSE/keep-alive 连接关闭，进程不退出；
- Rust 侧 sidecar::terminate 用无超时的 child.wait() 等待 Python 退出，
  阻塞在 RunEvent::ExitRequested 回调（Tauri 主事件循环线程）上，
  导致窗口无法销毁、进程无法退出。

修复（分层防御）：
- api_server.py: uvicorn 增加 timeout_graceful_shutdown=5
- sidecar.rs: unix terminate 改为 SIGTERM + 限时 try_wait 轮询，
  超 5s 则 killpg(SIGKILL) 兜底回收；新增 unix 回归测试验证
  SIGTERM 被忽略时能在 5s 内强杀回收。

fix(mcp): handle dataclass tool results in _make_jsonable

_make_jsonable only converted Pydantic BaseModel instances (via
model_dump), list, and dict. fastmcp's client auto-types
CallToolResult.data from a tool's output schema via
json_schema_to_type, which produces a plain stdlib dataclass (not a
BaseModel) whenever the schema doesn't set additionalProperties: true
-- the common case for a typical Pydantic-model tool return type. Such
an instance fell through to the final `return value` unconverted, so
json.dumps's `default` callback received the same unconvertible object
back and raised ValueError: Circular reference detected (its cycle
detector can't distinguish "default() gave up" from an actual cycle).

Adds a dataclasses.is_dataclass branch that recurses per-field (not a
raw asdict(), which would leave nested datetime/dataclass values
unconverted), plus a datetime/date branch, since a date-time schema
field validates to a real datetime object and would hit the same
failure one level down.

Reproduced against the real fastmcp dependency using an MCP tool's
output schema shaped like this (plain object properties, no
additionalProperties, nested datetime field): old _make_jsonable raises
the reported Circular reference detected error; the patched version
serializes correctly, verified both from direct construction and via
pydantic.TypeAdapter validation (the path fastmcp's client actually
uses).
